negative_reviews.author: Giulia F
negative_reviews.text: Food is very good, but it's a real shame that this place has such dirty toilets and a messy entrance. Even the pillows on the seats were stained and were turned upside down to hide the marks...! Despite being fairly new the space already looks so old and run down. My message to the manager: pay more attention to the details and cleaning, then this restaurant will be a great spot. But for now I wouldn't recommend it.

issues: Covers fell by 25 (4.88%) week on week while spend per head rose by £2.39 (6.02%), helped by the weather and a push on upselling.
Sales were about £20,400, £18,529.57 (47.51%) below target.
Maki Nori agreed with Matthew to lower the weekly target from £39,000 to about £24,000, awaiting Michael's final approval.
Labour rose slightly because a new employee was being trained.
Food stock tracking has improved; plant wine batches will be set up in Kobas with Ross to track vodka usage accurately and cut waste.
Kobas lists plum at £49 per kilo instead of £4.90, which needs fixing with Sophie.
A mandatory £10 per person deposit for Omakase bookings was set up with Ross to prevent no shows and food waste; Omakase nights run on Thursday and Friday.
Specials sold very well and all recent reviews were five star, despite a report showing an incorrect 2 star review; the KPI report notes no 2 star reviews last week.
The marketing material received was not usable because it lacked booking instructions and restaurant names, so the site will chase Georgina for a reprint.
Lunch promo marketing materials will go out on bill trays as a talking point to upsell the event.
Payroll was completed and onboarding records updated, but BOH employees cannot be seen in MAP, which Ziang Lin identified as a setup issue.
Compliance improved, although BOH staff still struggle to complete tasks; hygiene checks were at 100% compliance and all waste was tracked.
The bar was reorganised, moving soft drinks out of the freezer to make room for alcohol, and a new organic and vegan wine selection with better margins was introduced with Kei Cannon.
Contractors who painted the toilets left a mess on the mirrors and bins that needs cleaning up.
Table lamps ordered through Random Buy two weeks ago hit approval tracking issues; Kaitlin Docherty agreed to add Maki Nori to the Random Buy chat, where Kei Cannon approves orders every Wednesday.
Maintenance: there is a leak in the KP area.
Staffing: Beverly is doing well and getting fully trained, and the team is still being finalised.
Cleanliness is being worked on day by day, with a deep clean arranged for the coming days and pest control being monitored.
Next steps in the GM/HC notes: a kitchen cost plan with the head chef; the new Omakase material is not ready yet; reviews are better than last week but not yet enough.
Areas for improvement: service standards and more training, logistics and procedures, communication and a general meeting, upselling and spend per person, and cleaning.
Ziang Lin will visit Maki Nori on Friday.
No audit was done this week.

Region: the team aligned on implementing and keeping the dry ice presentation standard for volcano rolls and sashimi across sites: dry ice is poured at the table in a circular shape for volcano rolls, and sashimi is served on crushed ice in a red vegan ramen bowl with bamboo leaves and daikon to reduce dry ice waste.
